import os
import sys

import pytest

import click
from click.shell_completion import CompletionItem


class Foo(click.ParamType):
    def convert(self, value, param, ctx):
        return value

    def shell_complete(self, ctx, param, incomplete):
        return [
            CompletionItem(value=value, help="adsf")
            for value in ["baz:quux", "spam:eggs"]
        ]


@click.command()
@click.argument("foo", type=Foo())
def main(foo):
    click.echo(foo)


def _get_completions(cli, args, incomplete, prog_name="foo", shell="zsh"):
    """
    Helper function to get completions for a given CLI, arguments, and incomplete value.
    Mimics the behavior of the shell completion script.
    """
    complete_var = f"_{prog_name.upper()}_COMPLETE"
    os.environ[complete_var] = f"{shell}_complete"
    os.environ["_CLICK_COMPLETE_ARGS"] = " ".join(args)
    os.environ["_CLICK_COMPLETE_INCOMPLETE"] = incomplete

    comp_cls = click.shell_completion.get_completion_class(shell)
    comp = comp_cls(cli, {}, prog_name, complete_var)
    result = comp.complete()

    del os.environ[complete_var]
    del os.environ["_CLICK_COMPLETE_ARGS"]
    del os.environ["_CLICK_COMPLETE_INCOMPLETE"]

    return result.splitlines()


def test_zsh_completion_colon_in_value():
    """
    Test that zsh completion correctly handles values containing colons,
    displaying them as a single item rather than splitting them.
    """
    expected_completions = ["baz:quux -- adsf", "spam:eggs -- adsf"]
    actual_completions = _get_completions(main, [], "", shell="zsh")

    assert actual_completions == expected_completions
